samples.identification: StormAttack native loader with an erased resource directory
evidence: MSVC x86 PE. CRT entry VA 0x402674 reaches VA 0x401cb0. The configuration dword at VA 0x404120 is 3, selecting VA 0x401900 and shell cleanup VA 0x401390.

VA 0x401900 creates a GUID-named HKLM Active Setup Installed Components key, writes StubPath to a generated executable path, reads its own image, patches fields, writes a copy and invokes CreateProcessA on that path.
Alternate loader branches extract resource DLL/101 at VA 0x402460, write it at VA 0x4023c0, and replace LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL at VA 0x401260.

VA 0x401150 starts IE/notepad/calc, allocates remote storage for a DLL path, writes that path, resolves kernel32!LoadLibraryA, and passes that export and remote path to CreateRemoteThread at VA 0x40123d.
VA 0x401390 obtains the current module path and its short form, obtains COMSPEC, builds /c del with redirection to nul, and invokes CreateProcessA.

The 40960-byte resource section has 40959 null bytes and no valid resource tree. No live DDoS payload is present. Original fixed file offsets used by the self-copy patch no longer correspond to the flattened layout; retained hostile code is not proof of successful installation.

samples.identification: iOS activation-bypass utility infected by a native file-infector/downloader
samples.marker_note: Infected iOS bypass tool: correct resolver, DWARF and CBC traits
evidence: Go 1.22.3 Windows/386 program with module path bypass_no_change_sn and x/crypto v0.28.0. Go disassembly recovers main.runIdeviceinfo, SSH/SCP helpers, activation-record handling, device-setup changes and CBC file decryption: the host is an iOS activation utility.
The PE entry is redirected to VA 0xbb8000 in an appended writable section, file offset 0x769600. This graft is independent of the Go host and not an ordinary Go runtime stub.

VA 0xbb804d reads the PEB. Export-directory walking and immediate name comparisons resolve GetModuleHandleA, WinExec, CloseHandle, WriteFile, CreateFileA, GetTempPathA and lstrcatA. GetT here means temporary-path lookup, not timing.

VA 0xbb8059 patches an add-esp/jump continuation targeting original Go entry VA 0x46cf30. VA 0xbb81ee gets the temporary directory, appends a stack-built executable name, creates that file, searches up to 500 bytes for an inline MZ header, writes 0x3e00 bytes and launches the resulting path with WinExec.

The inline PE begins at file offset 0x769871. Its ASPack stub was unpacked in Unicorn with anonymous memory and stubbed allocation/loader APIs only; emulation stopped at original entry VA 0x4014e1. No native payload execution or real API/network calls occurred.

Unpacked VA 0x401099 constructs HTTP URLs, downloads staged files and launches them. VA 0x401e50 and following map target executables, add or replace a section, save and redirect the original entrypoint, write an entry graft and embedded image, and update/truncate the file. VA 0x402bb4 enumerates drives and VA 0x402aef enumerates files.

The bounded rotate/XOR decoder at VA 0x4017d0 reconstructs the configuration at VA 0x404288; it contains directory exclusions, a download host and a list of RAR payload names. These are downloader configuration, not proof of contact.

The Go host also links CBC support, but a generic cipher.NewCBCDecrypter/NewCBCEncrypter reference neither identifies AES nor proves completed encryption. DWARF section names similarly do not establish GCC authorship.

samples.identification: StormAttack native loader carrying a packet-tasked DDoS DLL
samples.marker_note: StormAttack loader and DDoS implant: no change
evidence: MSVC x86 PE shares the loader routines and mode-3 Active Setup/self-copy and shell-cleanup paths described for the first sample.

Resource DLL/101 at file offset 0x5060 contains 39936 bytes of a PE DLL. Its SHA256 is e58dd623e688da935eb785985f0c55ed8df09bd57567d8a2f6fdc10bf41511e1. Scanner carving includes following bytes, so its carved-child hash differs.

The DLL startup at VA 0x1000741a calls initialization VA 0x10007176, which on process attach starts worker VA 0x10006922. Connection logic at VA 0x1000693e invokes the binary-record handler VA 0x10006ac9.

VA 0x10006b45 receives up to 0x528 bytes, copies that record, then dispatches its leading dword. Task 5 passes a received record field to VA 0x100067c2, which resolves URLDownloadToFileA and launches the same destination via CreateProcessA.

The raw flood at VA 0x100022b6 calls WSASocketA(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, IPPROTO_UDP), enables IP_HDRINCL and repeatedly sends twelve-datagram bursts at VA 0x1000236b until a shared stop flag changes. Other task branches select additional traffic generators.
Storm DDOS Server/Storm Ser DLL resource identity, Storm banners and command format corroborate StormAttack; family attribution is not inferred from collector filename labels.

The near-null .htext section is a call/jump trampoline with NOP padding. No ransomware, credential theft or Remcos behavior was established. Loader code and DLL capabilities do not imply successful infection on a modern Windows host.

method: Independent static disassembly, Go symbol/call analysis, resource extraction and bounded CPU emulation; atomscan scores and collector labels were leads only.
external_sources: The three supplied tria.ge report URLs were inaccessible. No external verdict was used as proof.
changes: Corrected the x86 manual-name comparison description to describe the actual WinE/Clos/Writ/Crea/GetT prefixes, added an x86 architecture gate, and documented GetTempPathA rather than timing.

Moved the unchanged PE .debug_ section matcher from GCC compiler attribution to metadata/binary/debug::pe-dwarf-debug-section. Updated exact consumers and preserved effective DWARF exclusions/downgrades previously reached through compiler ancestors. Existing metadata/binary/ selectors already include it; ELF-only selectors cannot see it.

Moved generic CBC constructor references out of AES/library into crypto/encrypt and crypto/decrypt, retained notable severity, and removed the unsupported inherited encryption MBC mapping. Moved their direction-neutral consumer group to crypto/cipher and updated exact consumers.

CBC source scope now explicitly includes Go, repairing an existing Go-only consumer whose required constructor group had no reachable Go atom. Generic CBC intentionally no longer supplies AES identity to broad AES selectors.
Other traits in the two partially edited source catalogs remain unchanged. No sample-specific allowlists, filename conviction gates, new taxonomy leaves or inline YARA changes were introduced.

validation.atomscan_before_and_after: all three originals completed; original hostile/suspicious sets retained
